title: Leaders Can’t Make People Feel Safe
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article challenges the common assumption that leaders can directly create psychological safety, arguing instead that safety is a subjective perception team members build over time by testing how the organization reacts when they speak up or take risks. Leaders can only create the conditions where safety has a chance to emerge — setting the expectation that raising concerns is a core responsibility, modeling openness by admitting they don't have all the answers, equalizing airtime in meetings, and reacting calmly and with curiosity to disagreement. The piece stresses that safety isn't linear or permanent; consistency in how leaders react over time is what shapes the team's ongoing perception of how safe it actually is.
points: Safety is a subjective perception, not something a leader can grant directly through words alone.
Team members gauge safety by testing what happens when they speak up, and observing the consistency of leaders' reactions over time.
Leaders build the conditions for safety by setting clear expectations, admitting they don't have all the answers, and equalizing airtime in meetings.
Reacting calmly and with curiosity to disagreement, rather than assigning blame, reinforces perceived safety over time.
quotes: Contrary to what many leaders believe, they can’t make anyone feel safe.
What leaders CAN DO is to create the conditions where feelings of safety can emerge.
Because team members gauge their feelings of safety from the messages, decisions, and reactions they experience
Good leaders admit they don’t have all the answers and ask people to speak up when they see an issue or something overlooked.
A team environment is only as safe as people believe it to be.
